<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard package metadata and a `source` array pointing to the project's own Git repository over HTTPS. The `sha256sums` entry is set to 'SKIP', which is expected and acceptable for VCS sources in AUR and does not pose a risk during source fetching because the commands in question (`makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`) only download and extract sources without executing any build steps.

The `pkgver()` function executes during sourcing and runs `git describe` on the checked-out repository. This is a common pattern for -git packages and only operates on the already-fetched Git history. There is no evidence of malicious command substitution, network exfiltration, or execution of remote code in the top-level scope or `pkgver()`.

All operations performed during the specified `makepkg` commands are limited to cloning a public Git repository and extracting files — standard and expected behavior for AUR package building. No dangerous or unexpected code is executed at this stage.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Safe: standard VCS package with no malicious fetch-time behavior
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>

<details>
The provided `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file commonly used in Arch Linux AUR packages to describe the package's properties. It declares the source as a Git repository (`git+https://github.com/jamazi/jailbox.git`), which is consistent with the `-git` naming convention. The `sha256sums = SKIP` entry is standard for VCS (version control system) packages, as the checksum cannot be known in advance for mutable Git sources — this is normal and expected behavior, not a security risk.

All dependencies listed (e.g., `tor`, `iptables`, `iproute2`, `bash`) are legitimate system tools required for the described functionality of routing traffic through Tor with load balancing across exit nodes. There are no network downloads, executable scripts, or file modifications defined in this file. The `.SRCINFO` does not execute code; it only provides metadata for package building.

No malicious behavior is present. The file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices for a `-git` package. While the use of a mutable Git reference (as opposed to a pinned commit) may affect reproducibility, it does not constitute a security issue on its own, especially when sourced from the official upstream repository.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR metadata, no malicious content</summary>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a package named `jailbox-git` that aims to torify system traffic using multiple Tor exit nodes and load balancing. It pulls source code from the declared GitHub repository (`https://github.com/jamazi/jailbox.git`) via a git+https URL, which is standard for VCS packages in AUR. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is expected and acceptable for git sources, as content is inherently mutable and checksums cannot be pinned to a fixed release.

The build process consists solely of copying configuration files and scripts into appropriate system directories (`/etc/jailbox`, `/usr/bin`, `/usr/lib/systemd/system`). All installed files are part of the upstream source and serve clear roles: managing Tor configuration, defining service behavior, and providing control scripts. There are no network operations during build or install, no use of `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, or obfuscated commands, and no attempts to exfiltrate data or modify unrelated system components.

The package depends on standard system tools (tor, iptables, iproute2, bash) consistent with its purpose. Optional dependency on `obfs4proxy` supports pluggable transports, a legitimate Tor extension. Systemd service installation and backup of config files follow normal packaging practices. No red flags indicating supply-chain attacks or malicious behavior were found.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
No malicious code; standard AUR packaging practices observed.</summary>
</security_assessment>
